claims.text: The initial material is a powder-metallurgically produced AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 high-entropy alloy.
The initial AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 alloy has a multiphase microstructure.
The initial alloy lacks a purposely engineered lubricious surface oxide.
Post-sintering annealing in a slightly oxidizing atmosphere can deliberately form a continuous spinel oxide layer on the alloy.
The deliberately formed oxide layer will be thin and coherent.
The annealing treatment can produce a nanocrystalline spinel phase such as MnCr2O4-type oxide on the alloy surface.
The spinel oxide acts as a low-shear protective barrier.
The oxide layer minimizes direct metal-to-metal contact.
Low shear strength and coherent adherence of the oxide layer reduce friction.
The adherent oxide layer mitigates abrasive wear as service temperature varies.
Annealed samples will have a lower coefficient of friction than untreated samples across the target temperature range.
Annealed samples will have a lower wear rate than untreated samples across the target temperature range.
The treatment should remain effective in air from room temperature to approximately 900 degrees Celsius.
Optimizing annealing temperature, time, and oxygen partial pressure can promote continuous oxidation without degrading the substrate alloy.
Untreated high-entropy alloys typically have higher friction and wear rates, especially at elevated temperatures.
Uncontrolled oxide formation at elevated temperature causes inconsistent tribological behavior.
Tribological effectiveness requires the oxide layer to remain continuous and well adherent.
Extreme temperatures, excessive thermal cycling, or low oxygen availability can disrupt the oxide layer and compromise its effectiveness.

contradictions.description: The stated AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 alloy contains no Mn, yet MnCr2O4 is offered as an example of the oxide phase formed without identifying any external manganese source. An analogous spinel could be possible, but the specifically named Mn-bearing phase is compositionally inconsistent with the stated system.
